title: Duke researchers set to test agentic AI system for cardiovascular care
key_facts: A Duke team was awarded up to $15.5 million to help develop the first agentic AI system for cardiovascular care authorized by the FDA.
It is part of ARPA-H's ADVOCATE program, which has $62.7 million in total funding.
Three health-tech companies build the AI systems, Stanford builds a supervisory system against unsafe recommendations, and Duke with Kaiser Permanente tests them in real settings.
The AI is meant to autonomously support heart failure patients between visits.
Cardiovascular disease killed over 900,000 Americans in 2023 and nearly half of US counties have no practising cardiologist.
Duke expects to be ready to implement within a year and run a platform trial within two years.
Cost is unknown; researcher Rishikesan Kamaleswaran said 'a human is always going to be in the loop'.
quote_evidence: A Duke team of medical researchers has been awarded up to $15.5 million to help develop the first agentic artificial intelligence system for cardiovascular care authorized by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
“I think we’re going to learn about [pricing] as we do the implementation to see where the bottlenecks are,” Kamaleswaran said.
why_it_matters_hint: Could extend heart-failure care to places with no cardiologist, if it proves safe and affordable.
notes: The goal is FDA authorization; none exists yet. Single student-run outlet; award date not stated.
